content.value_statement: WordPress Interactivity API work can fail through hydration mismatches, missing directives, and unclear build setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through implementation, debugging, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Identifies Interactivity API usage through directive, store, and view module markers.
Guides setup for interactive blocks, themes, and plugin markup.
Explains server-side state, local context, and derived state patterns.
Troubleshoots hydration mismatches, inert directives, and missing module loading.
Aligns implementation choices with WordPress 6.9 directive behavior.
Suggests manual checks and end-to-end tests for interaction paths.
limitations: It does not run a WordPress site or browser test environment by itself.
It needs repository context, affected surfaces, and triage output for best results.
Guidance targets WordPress 6.9 and newer Interactivity API behavior.
It supplements official WordPress documentation but does not replace project-specific review.

use_cases.title: Fix Hydration Problems
use_cases.description: Diagnose mismatches between server-rendered markup and client-side state in interactive WordPress blocks.

use_cases.title: Add Interactive Theme Regions
use_cases.description: Plan directive processing, state initialization, and scoped markup for theme-level interactive regions.

use_cases.title: Review Plugin Interactivity
use_cases.description: Check existing plugin markup for directive conflicts, namespace mismatches, and WordPress 6.9 compatibility concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an interactive block.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WordPress block for Interactivity API setup. Check directives, store namespace, view script module loading, and server-rendered state.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Inert Directives
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging when clicks or bindings do nothing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug Interactivity API directives that do not respond. Inspect the markup, store actions, namespace, script loading, and console failure points.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Server Rendering
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation for stable first paint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a server-rendering plan for this interactive WordPress feature. Include initial state, local context, derived state, and hydration verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate For WordPress 6.9
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced compatibility review for existing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Interactivity API usage for WordPress 6.9. Find deprecated directives, page navigation assumptions, directive ID conflicts, and router region issues.

output_examples.input: A block shows hidden content before JavaScript loads.
output: Explains that server-rendered state may not match client expectations.
Recommends moving derived state into the server render path.
Suggests checking first paint and interaction behavior after the change.

output_examples.input: Two plugins need click behavior on the same element.
output: Identifies a possible directive attribute conflict.
Recommends unique directive IDs for each handler.
Suggests confirming both handlers fire in a smoke test.

output_examples.input: A theme needs an interactive menu without block metadata.
output: Creates a plan for manual directive processing.
Scopes state and context to the menu region.
Adds verification steps for loading, hydration, and navigation.

best_practices: Provide the affected block, theme, or plugin files before asking for implementation advice.
Share the WordPress version and build tooling so the skill can choose the right module path.
Verify changes with a manual interaction check and an end-to-end test when available.
anti_patterns: Do not add broad interactive roots when a smaller region can own the state.
Do not rely on client-only derived state when first paint depends on that value.
Do not ignore module loading, namespace matching, or console errors during debugging.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps build and debug WordPress Interactivity API features, including directives, stores, server rendering, hydration, and module setup.

faq.question: Does it require a specific WordPress version?
faq.answer: The guidance targets WordPress 6.9 and newer behavior, including deprecated directives and navigation changes.

faq.question: Can it create a new interactive block?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide setup, directive usage, state structure, view module wiring, and verification steps.

faq.question: Can it debug existing plugin markup?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect directives, namespaces, event handlers, state assumptions, and module loading paths.

faq.question: Does it run WordPress tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It suggests manual checks and end-to-end test coverage, but it depends on the project environment.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
